Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג: תנן, המקיף את חבירו מג' רוחותיו - אין מחייבין אותו. הא רביעית - מחייבין אותו. אימא סיפא: ר' יוסי אומר כו' וגדר את הראשונה כו' - אין מחייבין אותו - דהא לא אהני ליה מידי, שהרי גלוי הוא מצד רביעית. הא אם גדר עוד, מקיף את הרביעית - מחייבין אותו, דאהני ליה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:10:1.english: This is the text: We learned [in the Mishnah]: One who surrounds his neighbor on three sides... they do not compel him. [This implies that] for the fourth [side], they do compel him. Say [the same of] the latter clause: Rabbi Yosei says, etc. ... and he built a wall on the first, etc. - they do not compel him - For it has not benefited him at all, since he is still exposed on the fourth side. But if he built further, surrounding the fourth side, they compel him, for it has benefited him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:11:1.hebrew: אימא סיפא רבי יוסי אומר - בשלמא לרב הונא דאמר הכל דר' יוסי במה שגדר הוא, היינו דאיכא בין ת"ק לר' יוסי: דת"ק, דלא נקט לישנא דהכל, סבר דמי קנים בזול הוא דמחייבין אותו, ור' יוסי סבר כו'. דהא ליכא למימר דת"ק דוקא אם גדר מקיף את הרביעית הוא דמחייבין אותו, אבל אם גדר ניקף לא — דכ"ש הוא: השתא, היכא דלא גלי דעתיה דניחא ליה בהיקיפא קא מחייב ליה, כ"ש היכא דגלי. ולר' יוסי נמי קס"ד השתא דתנא ניקף, וה"ה למקיף, אלא בגלגול דהכל הוא דפליגי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:11:1.english: Say the latter clause: Rabbi Yosei says - Granted, according to Rav Huna, who said that the word "all" in Rabbi Yosei's statement refers to what he fenced, this is the difference between the first Tanna and Rabbi Yosei: The first Tanna, who did not use the language of "all," holds that they obligate him [to pay] only the price of reeds, at a cheap rate, while Rabbi Yosei holds, etc. For it cannot be said that the first Tanna obligates him only if he fenced the fourth side as the encloser, but if he fenced as the one enclosed, [he does] not [obligate him]. For it is a fortiori: now, where he did not reveal his intention that he is content with being enclosed, [the first Tanna] obligates him, all the more so where he did reveal it. And according to Rabbi Yosei too, we now assumed that he taught [the case of] the enclosed one, and the same applies to the encloser; rather, they disagree only about the extension implied by "all."

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:12:1.hebrew: אלא לת"ק דמי קנים נמי לא יהיב ליה אלא מאי יהיב ליה - מאי מחייבין אותו, דדייקינן ממילתיה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:12:1.english: Rather, according to the first Tanna, he does not give him the price of the reeds either; so what does he give him? - What do they obligate him [to give], which we infer from his words?

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:13:1.hebrew: יהב ליה אגר נטירא - דבר מועט שהיה צריך ליתן לשומר בכל שנה, כשהיא בקמותיה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:13:1.english: He gave him the payment for guarding - A small amount that he would have had to give a guard every year, while [the field] is standing in its crops.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:14:1.hebrew: דתנא קמא סבר - דמי רביעית יהיב ליה אם גדרה מקיף, אבל דמי הראשונות לא יהיב ליה, שכבר יצא מהם זכאי בבית דין, שהיו שם ימים רבים ולא הועילו לו. ואם גדרה ניקף לרביעית, לא יהיב ליה מידי, כדפירשתי, שכבר יצא ידי בית דין מהם. ולרבי יוסי, לא שנא גדרה ניקף ולא שנא מקיף, מגלגלין עליו את הכל בכולן דמי קנים:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:14:1.english: For the first Tanna holds - He pays him the cost of the fourth [wall] if the encircler built it, but he does not pay him the cost of the first [three walls], since he has already come out of them acquitted in court, as they stood there for many days and did not help him. And if the encircled party built the fourth, he gives him nothing, as I explained, because he has already fulfilled his obligation before the court with regard to them. But according to Rabbi Yosei, it makes no difference whether the encircled party built it or the encircler: they roll the whole [cost] onto him, for all of them, the cost of the [reed] stalks.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:15:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא מקיף וניקף איכא בינייהו - דתנא קמא אית ליה דרבי יוסי היכא דגדרה ניקף, אבל רבי יוסי לית ליה דתנא קמא בגדר מקיף. תנא קמא סבר: לא שנא ניקף ולא שנא מקיף, כי גדר לרביעית — מחייבין אותו, דהא תנא קמא במקיף איירי, ודייקינן ממילתיה הא רביעית מחייבין אותו, וכל שכן כשגדרה ניקף דגלי דעתיה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:15:1.english: And if you wish, say: [the difference between them is] the surrounder and the surrounded - For the first Tanna holds like R. Yose in a case where the surrounded one built the fence, but R. Yose does not hold like the first Tanna where the surrounder built it. The first Tanna maintains: There is no difference whether [it is] the surrounded or the surrounder; when he built the fence on the fourth side, we obligate him [to share in the cost]. For the first Tanna is speaking about the surrounder, and we infer from his wording that [in the case of] the fourth side, we obligate him, and all the more so when the surrounded one built it, since he has revealed his intention.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:17:1.hebrew: ור' יוסי סבר - דוקא גדרה ניקף, דגלי דעתיה; אבל גדרה מקיף, לא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:17:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds - [The rule applies] specifically where the one who was surrounded built the wall, since he revealed his intention [that he agrees to the partition]; but if the one who surrounded built it, [it does] not [count].

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:1:1.hebrew: נשעייה באמתא מלבר - יהא טח בטיט אמה בראש הכותל מבחוץ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:1:1.english: Let it be plastered with an amah [of plaster] on the outside - Let him plaster the top of the wall with a cubit [of] mortar on the outside.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:1:2.english: And he folds it - He folds it [over].

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:2:1.hebrew: הוצא - אם עשו מחיצת נצרים, כיצד יעשו חזית:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:2:1.english: Hotza (wicker fencing) - If they made a partition of wicker twigs, how do they make the chazit (the facing wall)?

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:2:2.hebrew: סינופי יריכי לבר - ראשי ההוצים ישב לצד שדה חבירו, וכשיהיה סונף ההוצים — כשיכלה האחד ויתן את חבירו — יסנפנו מבחוץ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:2:2.english: Attaching the ends from the outside - The tops of the hedge-thorns he sets toward his neighbor's field. And when he attaches the hedge-thorns, when one runs out and he adds the next, he attaches it from the outside.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:2:3.hebrew: הג"ה יריכי כדאמרי' לעיל טפח יתירא לביני אורבי תמ"ש - ור"ח פי' מוציא ראשי הקנים ודפנא, שהוא הקנים העומדים לחיזוק המחיצה לחוץ. מתוך פירושו משמע שהקנים שמעמידין מן הצד לסמוך הכותל, וזהו לשון סניפין. ע"כ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:2:3.english: Hagah of "yerichei," as we said above: "an extra handbreadth between the beams," etc. - And Rabbeinu Chananel explained: "He extends the tops of the reeds and the dafna," which are the reeds standing outside to strengthen the partition. From his explanation it implies that these are the reeds that are set up at the side to lean against the wall, and this is the meaning of the term "sinufin." End of his words.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:3:1.hebrew: אלא בשטרא - אם עשה האחד, יביא עדים ויחתמו לו, ואם עשהו שנים, יעידו עדים ויחתמו, דס"ל קופלא דטינא מעילויה הוצא לא ידיע:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:3:1.english: Except by a document - If one of them made it, he should bring witnesses and they should sign for him; and if two made it, witnesses should testify and sign. For he holds that the clod of clay on top of the *hotza* is not discernible.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:4:1.hebrew: ולא יעשו - חזית, לא לזה ולא לזה. והרי סימן שלא עשאה האחד בשלו, שאילו עשאה, היה עושה חזית מבחוץ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:4:1.english: And they may not make - a façade, neither for this one nor for that one. And behold, this is a sign that the one [who built the wall] did not make it on his own [land]; for if he had made it [on his own land], he would have made the façade on the outside.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:4:2.english: And he makes his own - He makes a façade on the outside.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:5:1.hebrew: ותקנתא לרמאי - בתמיה: וכי מפני דאגת רמאין איכפל תנא למיתני הא מתני'?
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:5:1.english: And [is it] a remedy for swindlers? - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question: Would the Tanna go to the trouble of teaching this mishnah because of concern for swindlers?

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:5:2.hebrew: ורישא - דקתני ״ועושה חזית מבחוץ״, לאו תקנתא משום רמאי הוא, דלא לימא חבריה ״של שנינו הוא״:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:5:2.english: And the first clause - Where it teaches, "and he makes a façade on the outside," this is not a remedy on account of a swindler. [It is rather stated so] that his fellow should not say, "It belongs to both of us."

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:6:1.hebrew: תנא דינא - הואיל ובקעה אין מנהג לגדור, אין יכול לכופו, אלא כונס לתוך שלו ובונה. ואיידי דתנא דינא, תנא תקנתא — ועושה חזית משום רמאי. אלא סיפא דינא לא תנא, דהא פשיטא דאם עשו מדעת שניהם, תעשה משל שניהם, וכולה משום תקנתא הוא דתנייה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:6:1.english: He taught the law - Since in a valley it is not the practice to build a fence, he cannot compel him [to contribute]; rather, he [the builder] draws in [the boundary] into his own [land] and builds. And since he taught the law, he [also] taught the remedy — that he makes a [partition] facing [the other's property] because of swindlers. But in the latter clause [of the mishnah] he did not teach the law, for it is obvious that if they made [the fence] with the consent of both, it is made from [the property] of both; and he taught all of it only on account of the remedy.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:1.hebrew: המקיף את חבירו משלש רוחותיו - שקנה ג' שדות סביב שדה חבירו לשלשת מצריה, וגדר את שלשתן, ונמצא שדהו של אמצעי זה מוקף משלש רוחותיו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:1.english: One who surrounds his neighbor on three sides - That he bought three fields around his neighbor's field, along its three boundaries, and fenced all three of them; and it turns out that the field of this middle [owner] is surrounded on three sides.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:2.hebrew: אין מחייבין אותו - לתת כלום. כדאמרי' דסתם בקעה מקום שנהגו שלא לגדור הוא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:2.english: We do not obligate him - to give anything, as we say that an unspecified valley is a place where they were accustomed not to build a fence.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:3.hebrew: הג"ה תמ"ש ול"נ טעמא משום דאכתי לא מהני ליה מידי, שהכל יכולים ליכנס מרוח רביעית. אבל אם גדר רביעית, מחייבין אותו, כדאמרינן בגמ'. ואע"ג דאמרינן לעיל דסתם בקעה מקום שנהגו שלא לגדור הוא, ה"מ בין בקעה לבקעה, וכותל גבוה ד' אמות לשם הוא דלא בעינן, מ"ט, דליכא היזק ראיה. אבל בשביל היזק בהמות שלא יכנסו לשדה, צריך לגדור גדר שלו עשרה טפחים, המונע מליכנס הבהמות:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:3.english: Gloss: [I am puzzled by what is written here,] and it seems to me that the reason is that [the one who fenced three sides] has still not gained anything, since everyone can enter from the fourth side. But if he fences the fourth side, they compel him [to share the cost], as we say in the Gemara. And although we said above that an ordinary valley is a place where it is customary not to fence, that applies only between one valley and another, and it is a wall four cubits high that we do not require there, because there is no damage of sight. But because of damage from animals, so that they will not enter the field, one must build his own fence of ten handbreadths, which prevents the animals from entering.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:4.hebrew: ה"ג ר' יוסי אומר אם עמד וגדר את הרביעית, ולא גרסי' ניקף:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:4.english: This is the text we read: "Rabbi Yose says: If he stood up and fenced the fourth [side]"; and we do not read "the one who was surrounded."

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:5.hebrew: הג"ה וכן בפירוש ר"ח ומיהו אניקף מפרשינן לה לקמן - תוס' והכי מוכח בפ"ב דב"ק, והלשון מוכיח דקתני "אם עמד" ולא קתני "אם גדר", מכלל דלאו בההוא דגדר השלש מיירי. ת' מו' שמ' ע"כ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:5.english: Gloss: And so [it is] in the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel, but nevertheless we explain it as referring to the one who was surrounded, below - Tosafot: And so it is proven in the second chapter of Bava Kamma, and the wording proves it, for [the Mishnah] teaches "if he stood" and does not teach "if he built a fence," which implies that it is not speaking of the one who built the three [sides]. [Signed:] ת' מו' שמ' — end of quote.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:6.hebrew: מגלגלין עליו את הכל - לתת חלקו בשלשת הראשונות, דכיון דגדר את הצד הפתוח, גלי דעתיה דניחא ליה במאי דגדר חבריה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:7:6.english: We roll the whole [cost] onto him - To give his share in the first three [sides]; for since he built [a wall on] the open side, he has revealed his mind that he is content with what his neighbor built.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:9:1.hebrew: לפי מה שגדר - בכל יציאות שהוציא בהן הראשון, יחזיר לו מחצה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:9:1.english: According to what he built - For all the expenses that the first one incurred on it, [the second] must repay him half.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:9:2.hebrew: דמי קנים - דאמר ליה: לדידי סגי לי בגדר קנים, ואי אפשי בהוצאה של גדר אבנים:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4b:9:2.english: The cost of reeds - For he [the one who was surrounded] says to him [the one who surrounded him]: For me, a fence of reeds suffices, and I do not want the expense of a stone fence.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:14:1.hebrew: שניה ושלישית לא - אומר ר"י: דהיינו טעמא, דאין לך אדם שלא היה מסייע לרביעית ע"מ שיהא גדור מד' רוחותיו. ובקונטרס פירש: לפי שכבר יצא מן השלשה מב"ד זכאי. הג"ה: וקצת קשה, דא"כ גם ברביעית יצא זכאי עד טפח אחרון, ע"כ:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:14:1.english: The second and third [years] not - Rabbi Yitzchak says: This is the reason — that there is no person who would not assist with the fourth [year] on the condition that it be enclosed on its four sides. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Because he has already left the three [years] of the court [proceedings] as acquitted. Gloss: And it is somewhat difficult, for if so, then also in the fourth [year] he would have left acquitted up to the last handbreadth. End of quote.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:17:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי סבר אם עמד ניקף וגדר את הרביעית - אע"ג דעד השתא היה מחמיר, כדמשמע לישנא ד"מגלגלין עליו את הכל" — להך לישנא לא הוי הכי, דלשון "אם עמד" משמע ניקף:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:17:1.english: "And Rabbi Yosei holds: if the surrounded one stood and built the fourth [wall]" - Even though until now he was stringent, as the wording "they roll everything onto him" implies — according to this version it is not so, because the expression "if he stood" implies [that it refers to] the surrounded one.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:17:2.hebrew: הגה"ה כתב בספרים אבל מקיף לא יהיב ליה אלא דמי רביעית - וקשה: דמנלן דיהיב ליה אפי' דמי רביעית? דילמא לא יהיב ליה כלל! וכן משמע בפ' כיצד הרגל (בבא קמא כ: ושם ד"ה טעמא), דקאמר: טעמא דניקף, הא מקיף פטור. ש"מ: זה נהנה וזה לא חסר — פטור. ודחי: שאני התם, דא"ל: לדידי סגי לי בנטירא בר זוזא. מיהו יש לדחות, דה"ק: לדידי סגי לי בנטירא בר זוזא, הלכך פטור מלסייע לד' רוחות; אבל רביעית יסייע, דאין לך אדם שלא יסייע לרביעית שיהיה גדור מארבע רוחותיו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:17:2.english: Gloss: It is written in the books: "But the encircler gives him only the value of a quarter" - This is difficult: From where do we know that he gives him even the value of a quarter? Perhaps he gives him nothing at all! And so it seems from [the Gemara in] the chapter "Keitzad HaRegel" (Bava Kamma 20b, s.v. ta'ama), which says: The reason [for liability] is that he is the encircled one; but the encircler is exempt. Learn from this that [in a case where] one benefits and the other does not lose, [the beneficiary] is exempt. And [the Gemara] rejected this: It is different there, for [the encircler] can say to him: "For me, a guard worth a zuz is enough." However, one can reject [this rejection], for this is what [the encircler] is saying: "For me, a guard worth a zuz is enough; therefore I am exempt from assisting with [the cost of fencing] four sides"; but he does assist with a quarter, for there is no person who would not assist with a quarter [of the cost] so that [his field] would be fenced on all four of its sides:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:2:1.hebrew: גייז ליה חבריה ושדי ליה - אע"ג דלעיל אמר: גזוזא מידע ידיע, בהוצא לא ידיע:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:2:1.english: His fellow can trim it off and throw it away - Even though above [the Gemara] said that trimmed-off pieces (gezuza) are recognizable, in the case of a projection (hotza) it is not recognizable.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:6:1.english: To exclude [the view of] Abaye - But Abaye holds that it is perfectly reasonable for [the Tanna] to teach a remedy for a swindler.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:7:1.hebrew: אם עמד וגדר את הרביעית - ל"ג "אם עמד ניקף", דהא לכולהו לישני דגמרא קאי אמקיף, בר מלישנא בתרא דקאמר "מקיף וניקף איכא בינייהו". והא דדייק בפרק כיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף כ: ושם): טעמא דניקף, הא מקיף פטור — היינו לההוא לישנא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:7:1.english: "If he stood and fenced the fourth [side]" - We do not read "if the surrounded one (nikaf) stood," for according to all the versions of the Gemara [the clause] refers to the surrounder (makif), except for the last version, which says, "The surrounder and the surrounded is the difference between them." And as for the inference that [the Gemara] draws in the chapter "Keitzad HaRegel" (Bava Kamma 20b, and there): [The ruling is] because of the reason of the surrounded one, [implying that] the surrounder is exempt — that is according to that version.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:9:1.hebrew: דמי קנים בזול - וא"ת: מאי שנא משדה שאינה עשויה ליטע, דאם נטעה חבירו שלא ברשות, אמר רב ושמואל בהשואל (ב"מ דף קא.): שמין לו, וידו על התחתונה? ואור"י: דשאני הכא, דמצי א"ל: לדידי סגי לי בנטירא בר זוזא. ומ"מ דמי קנים בזול יהיב ליה, דאנן סהדי דאם היה מוצאם כ"כ בזול היה גודר בהם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4b:9:1.english: The price of reeds at a discount - And if you ask: How is this different from a field that is not meant for planting, where, if one's fellow planted it without permission, Rav and Shmuel said in [the chapter] HaSho'el (Bava Metzia 101a) that they assess [the improvement] for him, and his hand is on the bottom [i.e., the planter receives the lesser of the two possible amounts]? And Rabbeinu Yitzchak answers: Here it is different, because [the owner] can say to him, "For me, a guard worth a zuz is sufficient." Nevertheless, he must give him the price of reeds at a discount, for we are witnesses that had he found them so cheaply, he would have built a fence with them:
